What creeps above…
Is it lost? Left behind?
Tired of drawing breath?
A Quiet One.
It's been so long since the last.
Let us see what it can do.
ROAN: They have come, master! From across the sea...

SELINE: My Inquisition is here as an act of mercy, Baron Winnick. There is an unholy presence 
on this island. I have come on behalf of King Magnus, who sent me —
WINNICK: A welcome sight though, aren't they? About time Phalen sent reinforcements.
ELLSWORTH: — King Magnus? The boy?
SELINE: I... forgive me. I thought you had heard.
SELINE: Your brother, the King... has passed.
ELLSWORTH: How long?
SELINE: It will be a week tomorrow.

SELINE: You should return to Phalen, Governor. Your nephew has 
extended his hand. He invites you to rejoin the family.
ELLSWORTH: Thank you, Madrigal. But Sacra is my home.
WINNICK: Fort Reach? Sacrament’s a bit out of your way then, isn’t it?
ROAN: It’s... an honor to meet you. I’ve only ever read the ancient texts about your kind.

SELINE: Sacra will be in capable hands. My Inquisition have quartered ourselves in Fort Reach, 
and will remain for as long as it takes to heal this island.

SELINE: My outfit encountered a group of raiders as we came ashore on your coast. 
We sent all of them to rejoin God... save one.
SELINE: I thought she might be of particular interest to you.
SELINE: We could have left her body by the side of the road, with the other animals.
SELINE: Consider this an offering of goodwill from the Church.

ODESSA: Where was the Church when our people were sick and starving? 
We’re done begging for scraps. We take what we need.
ELLSWORTH: Odessa. Don’t.

SELINE: Leave her. I’m sure the governor can properly discipline his own daughter.
At least as well as he governs his city...
ELLSWORTH: My apologies, Madrigal. It’s.. She does not stand for Sacrament.
ODESSA: Damn right I don't.
WATCHER: The Pestilence... it festers... Everything it touches...
ELLSWORTH: Guards! Take her away.
WINNICK: This way, Risen! ...I should have never taught you that little move.
SELINE: You will arrange an escort for my vanguard to Caylen.
ELLSWORTH: Caylen? ...It will be done. Is there anything else we can do?
SELINE: You can rejoice, Governor. Your salvation is at hand.
ROAN: Oh! The Inquisition at our gates, and Cerim in our rookery.
ROAN: We’ve prepared lodgings below. A humble room, to be sure, but safe and warm.
ROAN: I hope you’ve arrived in time to save our fair island. Not only in time to witness its ruin.
ROAN: Did you not hear? The Cerim have arrived!
WATCHER: They won’t come... Never answer...
ROAN: I... apologize. He was, is a brilliant scholar. But it’s been so long...
ROAN: God’s reach... They’re already here...
SELINE: Governor Ellsworth.

ELLSWORTH: Madrigal Seline. I apologize for the lack of a formal welcome. 
If you sent word, it must’ve been lost.
Gather in the Rookery
ROAN: You’ve arrived! I knew his letters were not in vain...
All players must gather in the Rookery
ELLSWORTH: Take the upper passage out, then leave by the northwest gate.
ELLSWORTH: Odessa.
ELLSWORTH: She wouldn’t have wanted this.
ELLSWORTH: Don’t be seen when you go.
ODESSA: What are you doing –
ELLSWORTH: Guard Benedus often sleeps on duty, and the ramparts above him will be unmanned.
ELLSWORTH: Head north to Irmgard in Marin. Or west to the Glades. Anywhere but here.
ODESSA: So that's it then.
ELLSWORTH: You have to go.
ODESSA: I was dragged through the gates in chains. I didn't ask to come here. Or are you too busy groveling to Phalen that you –
ELLSWORTH: Enough! Just go.
ODESSA: I was gone.
DARAK: You're fighting for a dead man.
DARAK: Ellsworth can't protect Sacrament. He can't protect anyone.
DARAK: Ellsworth arms field hands and farmers, and sends them to the slaughter.
DARAK: I wonder… By the time we breach Sacrament's gates…
DARAK: Will anyone be left inside?
RATTIGAN: There you are...
RATTIGAN: Your kingdom awaits within. And all the rot that comes with it.
RATTIGAN: Now we're square, me and you.
RATTIGAN: If you find Darak, tell him Rattigan sends his love...
DARAK: You're sick. All of you…
DARAK: Trying to stop me. To keep me from Annora…
DARAK: But I'll save her.
DARAK: Protect her. From…
DARAK: From you.
MAGNUS: This is my responsibility to the kingdom.
MAGNUS: With God’s hands, we will reach into every corner of the island.
MAGNUS: And bring it, like a newborn babe...
MAGNUS: Screaming into the light.
BAURUS: So it's true... The king is dead.
MAGNUS: Even now it ravages the island of Sacra, just off our own shores.
MAGNUS: Turning their men and women into... unspeakable things.
SELINE: The Pestilence is a punishment upon those who have lost their faith.
BAURUS: Is it now? How convenient.
SELINE: You question the Church?
BAURUS: You're not the Church, Madrigal. You're just the tip of its spear.
MAGNUS: Enough. Whatever the cause of this sickness, I cannot allow it to spread.
MAGNUS: My father has been... weak for many years. I will begin my reign doing what he could not.
BAURUS: My King, you are -- grieving. I must recommend against any --
MAGNUS: It's already done. Tomorrow, Madrigal Seline and her Inquisition will set sail for Sacra.
BAURUS: Long live the King.
SELINE: I promise we will cleanse the island of this wickedness.
SELINE: Our new king’s faith in the church is well placed.

BAURUS: Our king's faith was never in question. Ellsworth is a strong ruler, 
your grace. Sacra will recover.
MAGNUS: No. Sacra will be reborn.
BAURUS: He was a great man, and a good friend. I will mourn him.
SELINE: We will all mourn him.
SELINE: Your father's soul is at rest now, King Magnus. The people look to you for strength.
BAURUS: I offer my condolences, and my counsel, as I did for your father for many--
MAGNUS: The Great Pestilence has returned, Lord Baurus.
BAURUS: I... Yes, I have heard the rumors.
MAGNUS: They're not rumors.
ELLSWORTH: People of Sacrament. My people.
ELLSWORTH: History has called upon us. And history will remember how we answer.
ELLSWORTH: We find ourselves in a place we never sought - under the eyes of history.
ELLSWORTH: A plague that spent a thousand years confined to stories is now clawing at our gate.
ELLSWORTH: The threat of anarchy swells beneath us.
ELLSWORTH: God’s chosen descend from on high.
ELLSWORTH: And none of us can say what tomorrow will bring.
ELLSWORTH: But what I know is that our stone walls do not compare to the strength of our will.
ELLSWORTH: And I know both will withstand whatever rises against Sacrament...
ELLSWORTH: No matter the cost.
GUARD: Lower the bridge!
ELLSWORTH: Seek the Watcher, up in the Rookery.
WINNICK: Cerim. In the flesh and on our island... I thought you’d be taller.
ELLSWORTH: Your kind’s welcome within our walls. I trust you’ll find a home here.
ELLSWORTH: Welcome... to Sacrament.
WINNICK: State your business! Quickly! Don’t think just because you felled the beast you’re an ally.
ELLSWORTH: I apologize for the lack of hospitality. My friend here has his guard up for good reason.
ELLSWORTH: It’s alright, Winnick.

ELLSWORTH: Once the Raiders took the old fortress, their bloodshed has drawn 
more and more of those... things toward our city.
ELLSWORTH: ...My god. You’re Cerim.
ELLSWORTH: How did you manage to slay that monstrosity...
ELLSWORTH: The Watcher’s call has been answered.
WINNICK: Ha! I told that old coot he was wasting his time. For once I’m glad I was wrong.
Let the Gate stand as sentinel
Open when the world is in chorus
Closed when it cries out in torment
This is the will of the Sayer
RIVEN TWINS: Some of them begged…
RIVEN TWINS: Some of them prayed…
RIVEN TWINS: When we took their eyes, and cut their throats.
RIVEN TWINS: But there are no gods to answer.
RIVEN TWINS: ...Not even yours.
When I was a child…
Irmgard told me stories.
Said the Pestilence turned men’s faces inside out.
Made them grow limbs where none should be.
That the world was nearly lost in its wake.
And she prayed…
…that the Cerim would never need to return.
ODESSA: Let it burn! Show these mainlanders that Sacra is our island.
ODESSA: You shouldn't be here, Cerim!
ODESSA: It's too late for fairy tales.
ODESSA: It’s too late for any of us.
DECKHAND: We should turn back while we still can.
FIRST MATE: It’s an island. Not a fairy tale.
BOSUN: This is a fool’s errand. There’s no sum worth bringing the likes of them to shore…
Help me, Father…
Please… I didn’t run…
LARA: I'm still here!
ELLSWORTH: The hunters that escaped will be safe in Sacrament. I just hope we aren’t too late for our... guest.
WINNICK: I don’t like it. High walls, poor lines of sight. Good place for an ambush.
BAURUS: Passing? He was murdered. Poisoned by your nephew.
WINNICK: “King” Magnus needed his ass wiped until he was nine. You truly believe he could have –
BAURUS: Spoiled milk turns rotten. And little boys grow into tyrants.
ELLSWORTH: Those words are treason, Baurus. Not to be spoken lightly.
BAURUS: My loyalty is to the throne. Not who sits upon it.
BAURUS: You think it’s coincidence your brother’s body was barely cold before Magnus sent the Madrigal to your shores?
ELLSWORTH: The Church is here for the Pestilence, not our people.
BAURUS: For now. But there are few things more dangerous than a true believer.
WINNICK: I’ve no love for that zealot, but — Ellsworth can’t defy the Inquisition. That is madness.
BAURUS: The people will rally to you over that child.
ELLSWORTH: We’ll meet whatever comes, Winnick.
WINNICK: Follow him off a cliff they would. As would I. But this –
ELLSWORTH: Thank you for your warning, Baurus.
ELLSWORTH: I know you came here at great personal risk. But I won’t start a war.
BAURUS: You’re already in one, my friend. Pray you don’t realize that too late.
ELLSWORTH: Show yourself! I take no counsel from those who lurk in the shadows.
BAURUS: And what about old friends?
ELLSWORTH: Lord Baurus...
WINNICK: You old fool! Why all this cloak and dagger? The Master of Trades is always welcome in Sacrament.
BAURUS: Phalen’s eyes are everywhere. And I doubt the Royal Court would approve my coming.
ELLSWORTH: Yes, we heard of his passing.
BAURUS: Governor. I have news about your brother.
